## IBrokerageAccountIdentity

Source: [src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/IBrokerageAccountSync.cs:17](../../../../src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/IBrokerageAccountSync.cs#L17).

Source: [src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/IBrokerageRetainedOrderRecoveryGateway.cs:11](../../../../src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/IBrokerageRetainedOrderRecoveryGateway.cs#L11).

Order recovery that takes the retained order&#x27;s identity and the connection generation the caller bound its recovery scope under, for a gateway that matches by a client-supplied reference: a different instrument, side or type under the same reference is refused before any route is installed for the match, and a lookup is refused outright, installing nothing, when the connection has changed since the scope was bound. ## IRiskReservation

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Execution.Sdk.IRiskReservation</code>. Kind: `interface`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/RiskContracts.cs:119](../../../../src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/RiskContracts.cs#L119).

Capacity held for one in-flight evaluation by a rule that consumes a finite resource (rate windows, burst counters). Exactly one of Commit or Rollback takes effect; both are idempotent so a cleanup path can settle unconditionally without double-settling. Ownership moves: the validator rolls reservations back if evaluation throws or is cancelled, and transfers them to the caller on a normal return. Only the caller commits, and only once the order has actually been routed.

```csharp
public interface IRiskReservation
```

Declared public members:

| Declaration | Source | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>void Commit();</code> | [src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/RiskContracts.cs:122](../../../../src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/RiskContracts.cs#L122) | Keeps the reserved capacity — the order was routed. |
| <code>void Rollback();</code> | [src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/RiskContracts.cs:137](../../../../src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/RiskContracts.cs#L137) | Returns the reserved capacity — the order was blocked, was cancelled before dispatch, or definitively failed before reaching the venue. Not for an ambiguous submission failure. When a gateway call throws after dispatch may already have happened, the order may still execute, so the caller commits instead: for a rate limiter the safe direction is to over-count. Under-counting would let a runaway algorithm bypass the ceiling by producing ambiguous submissions, which is the behaviour the control exists to stop. Roll back only when nothing can have reached the venue — a rejection, a duplicate client order id, a gateway report of Rejected, or a cancellation observed before the gateway was called. |

## KillSwitchSweepResult

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Execution.Sdk.KillSwitchSweepResult</code>. Kind: `record`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/KillSwitchSweepResult.cs:42](../../../../src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/KillSwitchSweepResult.cs#L42).

The outcome of a kill-switch cancel-all sweep, per order rather than in aggregate. This type exists because the sweep used to report success by completing. It awaited a cancellation for every order and discarded each result, so a broker that refused one cancellation left that order working while the sweep returned normally and the audit trail recorded Completed. The exit criterion is that activation cancels open orders, which a call that merely ran cannot establish — so the sweep now reports what it actually achieved, and names what it did not.

```csharp
public sealed record KillSwitchSweepResult(KillSwitchSweepOutcome Outcome, int Requested, int Cancelled, IReadOnlyList<KillSwitchSweepFailure> StillWorking)
```

Distinct from Outcome because the two failures call for different operator responses: StillWorking names orders to cancel by hand, while this flag means the broker may hold orders the sweep never even saw — after an OMS restart or for legs the OMS does not track — and the broker book must be verified directly. |
